title: SE/ProServices integration deep-dive & velocity review - 2027-09-02
content:
Attendees: Aisha (SE lead), Miguel (ProServices PM), Ravi (SRE), Hannah (Field Eng), Jonah (Customer Success)

Goal: quick velocity review + one deep-dive on priority customer blockers. Keep to 45 min. Capture owners and next checkpoints.

Agenda:
- 5m: Quick wins / throughput metrics
- 20m: Deep-dive: Monarch Retail integration (accuracy regression + deploy flakiness)
- 10m: Smaller customer highlights (Cobalt Labs, Nimbus AI, Sable Financial)
- 10m: Actions, risks, next sync

1) Quick velocity snapshot (Miguel)
- This sprint (Aug 28 - Sep 02): 9 integration milestones closed (down from 14 last sprint). Throughput of onboarding tasks per engineer = 0.8 (target 1.2).
- Main slowdowns: extra certificate rotations, customer QA cycles, and SRE backfills.
- Quick wins: new onboarding checklist template applied to 3 customers cut followup time by ~12%.

2) Deep-dive: Monarch Retail (HIGHEST PRIORITY)
Summary of problem:
- Customer reported: generated product descriptions are inconsistent after final quantized model rollout. Some short prompts return garbage tokens or repetitive outputs. Also occasional 502s during heavy batch replay.
- Timeline: issue first seen 2027-08-26 after we promoted q4-epoch-compact to dedicated pool in us-east-1. 2 stage rollout (canary -> full) completed on 08-27.
- Impact: blocking their consumer-facing feed. Rolling back to previous variant reduced noisy tokens but still saw degraded latency under load.

Technical notes (Ravi / Hannah):
- Preliminary analysis: reproducer shows mismatch in KV cache format when switching between non-quantized and quantized variants at request-level. The runtime accepts cached prefixes from non-quantized sessions but the kernel path for quantized model handles attention differently -> leading to corrupted token probabilities for some position offsets.
- Also observed increased GPU memory pressure when serving q4-epoch-compact at sequence lengths >1024 due to a fallback to non-optimized attention kernel (driver: cuda 13.1, runtime-serve v2.9.1).
- 502 root cause: autoscaler spawn race + ephemeral Nginx upstream healthcheck mismatch (healthchecks too aggressive during cache warming).
- Logs: linked artifact GITHUB:rw-infra/kv-cache-fix#214 contains reproducer scripts and sample traces.

Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Hotfix 1 (Ravi): disable cross-variant prefix reuse for Monarch only (apply request header override). Rollout window: 09-03 02:00-04:00 UTC. Risk: increased token cost, but reduces corruption.
- Hotfix 2 (Hannah): pin to q3-standard variant for traffic >=75% until kernel fix lands. Must coordinate with Monarch PM and product to accept transient latency increase.
- Hotfix 3 (Miguel + Jonah): schedule coordinated QA window and cutover plan with Monarch for 09-04. Include synthetic load ramp to observe 502s.

Longer term fixes (SRE + Runtime):
- Merge patch that normalizes KV cache serialization across quantization variants (PR 214). Target milestone: 2.10.0 release (ETA 2027-09-10).
- Add proactive monitoring for attention kernel fallback events and sequence-length-triggered kernel selection.
- Tune autoscaler healthcheck grace + implement staggered warm-up for new replica pools.

Open questions for product/ops:
- How aggressive are we willing to be on per-customer variant pinning? (tradeoff: unit cost vs. stability)
- Do we enforce a canary delay of 48h for quantized variants with new kernels?

Action items (owners / due):
- Aisha: Draft Monarch customer-facing incident note + rollback rationale (due 2027-09-03)
- Ravi: Deploy cross-variant prefix reuse toggle for Monarch and monitor for misdecoded tokens (due 2027-09-03 06:00 UTC)
- Hannah: Coordinate with runtime team to validate PR 214 in staging and produce perf numbers (due 2027-09-07)
- Miguel: Schedule Monarch QA cutover with their PM & send runbook (due 2027-09-03)
- Jonah: Prepare synthetic load scripts and share in GITHUB repo by 2027-09-02 EOD

3) Customer highlights (10m)
- Cobalt Labs: stuck on SAS token rotation for private deployment; customer tenant is passing tests but failing egress policy verification. Owner: Miguel -> next checkpoint 2027-09-06.
- Nimbus AI: finished initial batch of evals; recommended quantization profile q3-standard for embeddings (reduced 28% cost w/ <1% quality delta). Owner: Hannah.
- Sable Financial: compliance team asked for extra audit logs; legal review in progress. Jonah to loop in security for evidence package.

4) Operational notes / capacity planning (Ravi)
- Dedicated pool capacity in us-west-2 has 18% spare GPU-hours this week; consider shifting small customers to that region to alleviate us-east burstiness during Monarch remediation.
- Suggest temporary quota increase for ProServices trial projects for next 2 weeks to accelerate onboarding.

5) Retro & process improvements (Aisha)
- Observed pattern: quantized rollout discoveries are happening post-canary. We should add a small synthetic workload test that forces cross-variant prefix reuse in canary phase.
- Introduce a short checklist item: "validate KV cache cross-variant compatibility" on all model rollout PRs.

Next sync: 2027-09-09 16:00 UTC (45 min). Propose deep-dive follow-up only if main hotfixes do not stabilize.

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep Monarch updates high-priority in Slack thread and mark incidents if any customer-visible errors occur.
- Need to push runtime team to add kernel selection metrics to the console.

Appendix: quick links (copied here so doc is stand-alone)
- Reproducer & traces: GITHUB:rw-infra/kv-cache-fix#214
- Rolling plan template: CONFLUENCE-8321
- Incident runbook: JIRA:SE-1198

End of notes.
